```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
has_dfms <- requireNamespace("dfms", quietly = TRUE)
```

`rinow` organises a nowcasting system in three steps: data with a release
calendar, model specifications, and pseudo real-time evaluation. This vignette
uses simulated data; the same code works on the Indonesian example
`idn_nowcast`.

## Data and vintages

```{r}
library(rinow)
sim <- simulate_nowcast_data(n_years = 16, seed = 11)
sim
v <- vintage(sim, "2015-08-20")
ragged_edge(v)
```

`vintage()` keeps only what was released by the information date, so the
indicators end in different months: this is the ragged edge.

## Models

Every model is a specification object; `nowcast()` applies it to a vintage.

```{r}
models <- list(ar_model(), bridge_model(c("x1", "x2")), midas_model(c("x1", "x3"), n_lags = 3),
               factor_model(c("x1", "x2", "x3")))
res <- lapply(models, nowcast, data = v, target = "2015Q3")
do.call(rbind, lapply(res, as.data.frame))
```

A bridge nowcast splits into contributions:

```{r}
plot(res[[2]])
```

```{r, eval = has_dfms}
nowcast(dfm_model(c("x1", "x2", "x3")), v, "2015Q3")
```

## Pseudo real-time evaluation

```{r}
s <- nowcast_schedule("2011Q1", "2015Q2")
ev <- lapply(models, evaluate, data = sim, schedule = s)
ev <- c(ev, list(combine_nowcasts(ev, method = "mean")))
accuracy(ev)[, c("model", "position", "rmse", "mae", "n")]
dm_test(ev[[2]], ev[[1]])
```

Accuracy improves from `M1` to `B` as more of the quarter's data arrive; the
Diebold-Mariano test compares the bridge equation with the AR benchmark.

## Interface

`run_app()` opens a step-by-step 'shiny' interface (Indonesian by default,
`run_app("en")` for English) that covers the same workflow and exports an R
script reproducing the analysis.
